motor_name: Problem Formalization / Expert Problem Spec Engine

summary.verdict: The implementation conforms to the Problem Formalization / Expert Problem Spec Engine contract. It consumes activated inference cases with authorized phase contracts, dependency version records and canonical taxonomy mappings; emits ExpertProblemSpec, AmbiguityRegister and ParameterConstraint records; preserves provenance, lineage and deterministic version metadata; blocks unresolved critical ambiguity; and keeps all emitted objects non-evidentiary with intended_use=exploration.

findings: Inputs match the functional contract: inference_cases must be a list, phase_contracts must be a mapping, version_records must be a list, canonical_taxonomy must be a mapping, and each accepted case must be active, identified, phase-authorized and provenance-backed.

Outputs match the contract: each accepted case produces one ExpertProblemSpec, one owning AmbiguityRegister and the expected ParameterConstraint records, all tied to the same source_problem_ref and spec_id lineage.

The implementation rejects inactive cases, missing provenance or dependency version records, invalid phase authority, invalid problem classes and unresolved critical source ambiguities with structured motor_029 errors.
Taxonomy boundaries are enforced: target variables and parameter names must resolve through canonical taxonomy or become explicit ambiguity items instead of local labels.

Synthetic-chain epistemic rules are enforced on runtime outputs: ExpertProblemSpec, AmbiguityRegister and ParameterConstraint records carry non_evidentiary_flag=true, intended_use=exploration, source_problem_ref, domain_validity_limits and limitations_note.

The output whitelist preserves motor scope by rejecting forbidden fields associated with synthetic datasets, generation manifests, training runs, selected models, metrics, rankings or field-validation results.

ExpertProblemSpec records include source_problem_ref, phase_contract_ref, taxonomy_snapshot_ref, version_record_refs, lineage_refs, provenance_refs, source_ref, produced_by_motor, produced_at, parent_id, version_id and version_hash.
AmbiguityRegister records preserve register_id, spec_id, source_problem_ref, blocking_item_refs, handoff_allowed, non-evidentiary flags, lineage anchor fields and deterministic version metadata.

ParameterConstraint records include constraint_id, canonical_term_ref, value_type, structured allowed_domain, unit handling, rationale, uncertainty_treatment, compatibility_refs, source_ref, produced_by_motor and version metadata.
Stable identifiers and version hashes are derived from normalized material content and source references, with runtime timestamps excluded from material hash comparison.
Supersession uses parent_id linkage for prior records rather than silent mutation of upstream inference cases, phase contracts, version records, taxonomy terms or prior specs.

test_results.coverage_assessment: The documented test specification covers happy path, sparse case, malformed input, edge cases, pass criteria and fail criteria. A no-bytecode executable smoke exercise ran eight checks against the implementation: happy path output shape and flags, deterministic rebuild hash stability, sparse case without invented parameters, unknown required taxonomy term blocking handoff through ambiguity, inactive case rejection, missing version lineage rejection, unresolved critical ambiguity rejection and invalid problem class rejection.
test_results.notes: No standalone test runner or implementation file was changed during conformance review. The smoke exercise imported the implementation with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 to avoid writing cache files and used the documented phase contract, version record, taxonomy and case shapes from the artifacts.
